Las moléculas del agua líquida se escapa: The molecules of liquid water escape into the air as vapour, and the hotter the water, the more vapour there is and the more it presses. Water boils when the pressure of its vapour equals the pressure on top of it: then vapour also forms inside the liquid, as bubbles.\n\nAt sea level the air pressure is 1 atm = 101.3 kPa and that equality occurs at 100 °C. It is not a property of water alone: it depends on the pressure above it.
En la montaña el agua hierve antes: In the mountains water boils sooner
hierve el agua en la cima, a unos 31 kPa: water boils at the summit, at about 31 kPa.
Cuanto más subes, menos aire tienes enci: The higher you go, the less air you have above you and the less it weighs: in Madrid, at 650 m, it is 93 kPa; on Everest, at 8849 m, only about 31 kPa, almost a third of an atmosphere. The water vapour equals that pressure much earlier, at about 70 °C.\n\nThat is why in the mountains pasta takes longer to cook, even though the water is "boiling": it boils, but at a lower temperature, and it is the temperature that cooks. A thermometer that measures when water boils can even serve as an altimeter.
La olla a presión sube la presión: The pressure cooker raises the pressure
hierve el agua dentro de una olla a pres: water boils inside a pressure cooker.
La olla hace lo contrario que la montaña: The pressure cooker does the opposite of the mountain. With the lid closed, the steam that comes off the water cannot escape, so it builds up and the pressure rises until a valve lets it out. In a household cooker it is about 2 atm, one above that of the air.\n\nWith double the pressure on top, the water has to be hotter for its vapour to match it: it boils at about 121 °C. The water keeps boiling, but at a temperature that an open saucepan can never reach.

Cocer es una reacción química (los almid: Cooking is a chemical reaction (starches gelatinise, proteins denature, collagen softens) and its rate grows greatly with temperature: as a rough rule, it doubles every 10 °C.\n\nFrom 100 °C to 121 °C is about 21 °C and $2^{2.1} ≈ 4.3$: what takes an hour in the saucepan, the pressure cooker does in about 14 minutes. It is also an energy saving, because it is heated for less time.
